messages:
maria: heads up — release pipeline failed on the typegen/regeneration check for v1.12.0.
maria: CI is blocking npm/pypi publish because files in `packages/sdk/types` changed but we didn't intend an API change.
alex: ugh. I saw that. openapi-codegen output changed enum ordering, which made typegen reorder constants. not a real breaking change but CI expects a semver bump if types change.
jonah: can you paste the regen diff? might be whitespace or ordering only.
maria: here you go:
```
$ git --no-pager diff -- packages/sdk/types
diff --git a/packages/sdk/types/models.ts b/packages/sdk/types/models.ts
index e3a4b1c..f9d7c2a 100644
--- a/packages/sdk/types/models.ts
+++ b/packages/sdk/types/models.ts
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ export enum SortOrder {
-  Asc = 'asc',
-  Desc = 'desc',
+  Desc = 'desc',
+  Asc = 'asc',
 }
```
maria: CI treats any diff as requiring a release, and the semantic-release step then fails because we didn't update changelog/semver in PR.
alex: that's the core problem — our regen is non-deterministic across runs. sometimes codegen emits different enum order depending on hash of openapi components.
jonah: we had a flaky generator reported months ago. thought we fixed stable sorting, but maybe some deep-of components still iterate maps.
maria: publish-bot posted:
```
publish-bot: publish blocked — regen diff detected. Please commit regenerated files or mark as docs-only with [skip-regenerate].
```
alex: marking as docs-only feels risky. If a downstream sample app relied on the enum order (it shouldn't), this hides a real change.
jonah: agree. short-term: we should revert the PR that changed the OpenAPI spec ordering, regen locally, commit deterministic output.
maria: tried that — local regen still flips order. I compared generator versions between my laptop and CI; both use the same docker image.
alex: can we add a post-process sort step in the typegen pipeline? like stableSortEnums() before writing files.
jonah: yes, and also add a test in CI that runs regen twice and asserts no diff, so we catch nondeterminism in PRs.
maria: created a quick patch: added deterministic sort for object keys + enum members. CI rerun now — still failing but a different file this time (models -> client.ts imports order).
alex: that's the maddening part — multiple sources of nondeterminism: map iteration, glob ordering, and filesystem timing.
jonah: plan:
- add stable sort util to codegen core (ensures deterministic AST output)
- add double-regenerate check in CI (regen, regen again, git diff == empty)
- relax release gating to allow docs-only regen if we can annotate PRs clearly
- temporarily disable semantic-release auto publish until we clear the churn
maria: I like the double-regenerate check. Quick patch: in .github/workflows/regen.yml add step:
```
- name: regenerate twice
  run: |
    make regenerate
    make regenerate
    git --no-pager diff --exit-code || (echo "regen non-deterministic" && exit 1)
```
alex: add that, and a unit test that runs `node scripts/stable-sort.js` over fixtures.
jonah: also update CONTRIBUTING.md: ask maintainers to run `yarn regen && git status --porcelain` before merging.
maria: side issue — semver policy: semantic-release wants to bump minor on any type change. We should document exceptions for purely ordering-only changes. otherwise changelog filled with noise.
alex: agree. propose: only treat API surface-level signature changes as minor/major. Ordering reformatting should be patch.
jonah: that requires annotating the regen diff detection script to heuristically classify diffs: type ordering changes -> patch. Might be ok for now.
maria: for the immediate release, I force-pushed a commit with the regenerated files from the deterministic patch; CI passed on the regenerate check but semantic-release still wanted a version bump.
alex: manual workaround: edit CHANGELOG.md with a small patch entry and re-run release, then we can revert once pipeline is fixed.
jonah: please add an issue to track full fix and link PRs. I'll queue the stable-sort PR and the CI double-run.
maria: filed ISSUE: https://redwood-internal/issue/5236 — title: "Make codegen/typegen deterministic + CI double-regenerate check" and attached failing logs.
alex: thanks. small follow-up: add a smoke test that boots example/sample-app using the packaged sdk to ensure sample apps don't break on published packages.
maria: noted. I'll follow up with a PR that: stable sort + CI check + smoke tests. tagging @jonah for review.
jonah: will review today. thanks for the triage, team :tada:
ci-bot: build #3421 passed after regen commit — publish queued.
publish-bot: published @redwood/sdk v1.12.0 — success.
maria: closing thread — let me know if you see weird behavior in sample apps.
alex: nice recovery. :thumbsup:
jonah: closing — keep an eye on flaky codegen tests.
